title: Hosted API streaming: KV-lock cascade and circuit-breaker synthesis
content:
Summary:

This is a combined incident review and runbook-draft for the P0 hosted-API streaming outage on 2027-04-08 that produced widespread token emission stalls and a short 5xx wave. The root cause was a cascade triggered by KV-cache lock contention across cross-region prefix invalidation, amplified by a too-aggressive circuit-breaker config in the streaming proxy. Impacted customers saw stalled streams (no tokens for 5–30s) and intermittent 502/503s during automatic fallback.

Scope & impact:
- Severity: P0 (hosted API streaming, customer-facing).
- Time window: 2027-04-08 13:14 - 2027-04-08 13:49 UTC (degraded until soft rollback at 13:49; final mitigations landed at 14:20).
- Affected surfaces: streaming endpoints for text generation (streaming clients experienced long token pauses), a small fraction of non-streaming requests saw transient 5xx as proxy retries failed.
- Customer-visible symptoms: long pauses between chunks, some streams terminated with 5xx, increased fanout latency and error rate.

Detection and alerts:
- First alert: automated streaming-latency SLO alert at 13:16 (p95 chunk latency breached 3s threshold).
- Pager routed to on-call SRE (Asha) and streaming-service owner (Ethan).
- Secondary signals: sudden spike in KV-cache contention metrics (lock_wait_count, lock_hold_ms), elevated proxy circuit-breaker trips for streaming-paths.

Timeline (condensed):
- 13:14 UTC: small config push to cache-invalidator service (region failover test) partially rolled; invalidation messages increased cross-region prefix churn.
- 13:15–13:17: KV cache experienced a surge of invalidation/reload ops; lock_wait_count climbed x15.
- 13:17–13:22: Streaming runtime started queuing requests waiting for KV loads; emission loop blocked behind KV lock for some prefixes, leading to token stalls.
- 13:18–13:25: Edge streaming proxy observed higher tail latencies and started tripping its circuit-breaker (configured to protect backends); trips caused immediate 502s for some sessions and routed others to fallback synchronous path.
- 13:25–13:40: Feedback loop: client retries and fallbacks caused extra load on control-plane fetches and on fallback model instances; telemetry showed elevated CPU on model pools.
- 13:40: Temporary mitigation (#1) — disabled aggressive invalidation path (rollback of the config push) and relaxed KV loader lock policy (soft patch) in staging then prod.
- 13:49: Streaming service rollback to previous invalidation routing completed; circuit-breaker thresholds temporarily widened to reduce false trips.
- 14:20: Permanent mitigations and instrumentation (see follow-ups) deployed to prod.

Root cause analysis (why):
1) Operational change: the config push intended to improve cross-region consistency introduced a new invalidation fanout path which created high-frequency prefix invalidations during certain failover patterns.
2) Architectural blind spot: KV-loader uses a coarse-grained prefix lock to prevent duplicated loads; under high invalidation churn, many streams contended on the same lock leading to emission stalls.
3) Protection misconfiguration: streaming proxy circuit-breaker thresholds were tuned for latency protection but not for transient KV-blocking behavior; breakers tripped early and amplified user-visible errors instead of allowing degraded streaming.
4) Insufficient observability: lock-level metrics existed but lacked per-prefix histograms and alerting that would have detected abnormal skew quickly.

Why the cascade happened:
- Lock contention caused per-session stalls (long tail), which clients retried or wrote more control-plane requests. Those retries increased pressure on the invalidator and model pools. The streaming proxy saw increased per-call latency and tripped breakers, turning stalls into 5xx for some clients.

Immediate remediation (what we did during incident):
- Rolled back the recent invalidation routing change (13:40–13:49).
- Temporarily relaxed circuit-breaker thresholds on streaming proxies to prefer degraded streaming over hard 502/503 (13:49).
- Applied a temporary KV-loader backoff to serialized reloads to reduce thundering (13:55).
- Throttled client retry traffic at edge where safe to do so (14:00).

Runbook draft (playbook for similar incidents):
- Pager escalation: SRE on-call + streaming service owner + infra lead.
- Quick checks (first 5 minutes):
  1) Confirm alert type: p95 chunk latency vs 5xx spike.
  2) Check invalidator config status: recent pushes in last 60m (gitops UI / deploy logs).
  3) Fetch KV-lock metrics: lock_wait_count, lock_hold_ms, per-prefix hot keys (if available).
  4) Inspect proxy circuit-breaker dashboard: trip count, last trip timestamps, configured thresholds.
- Fast mitigations (order matters):
  A) If invalidator / config push present: rollback to previous commit (gitops rollback) and confirm message queues drain.
  B) If KV-lock waits high: enable KV-loader serialized backoff / staggered retries for hot prefixes (config flag: kv.loader.backoff=true).
  C) If circuit-breakers tripping: widen breaker thresholds for streaming path (increase consecutive_failure threshold and reduce failure window) and set to half-open faster.
  D) If client retries observed: apply edge retry rate-limit for streaming route (edge rate-limit for 'streaming-chunk' route).
- Commands & snippets used during incident (on-call notes):
  - Check deployments: kubectl -n streaming get deploy -o wide | grep invalidator
  - Inspect queue backlog: kc exec -n infra invalidator-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'redis-cli llen invalidation_queue'
  - Check locks: curl -s http://kv-metrics.prod.internal/locks | jq '.|{waits: .wait_count, hold_avg: .hold_ms}'
  - Rollback gitops: fluxctl rollback --namespace=streaming invalidator-controller --to=HEAD~1
  - Relax breakers: curl -X POST "https://proxy-admin/adjust?path=/v1/streaming&cb_threshold=10" -H"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

Telemetry & dashboards to add (short-term):
- Per-prefix lock wait histogram and top-10 hot prefixes in the SRE dashboard.
- Streaming token emission gap telemetry (distribution of inter-token gaps per session).
- Circuit-breaker trip reason labels (KV-lock vs backend-5xx vs network).
- Alert rule: composite alert that fires when p95 chunk latency > X AND lock_wait_count > Y for 5m.

Longer-term engineering actions (owners & ETA):
- Engineering (Maya) — Replace coarse-grained KV prefix lock with per-key async loader (SRE-2360). ETA: Q3 2027.
- Infra (Luis) — Add backpressure token to invalidator fanout pipeline to rate-limit cross-region churn (SRE-2361). ETA: 6 weeks.
- Proxy team (Ethan) — Implement breaker heuristics aware of KV-blocking label so breakers deprioritize transient KV stalls (PROXY-879). ETA: 8 weeks.
- SRE (Asha) — Add per-prefix lock histograms and composite alerting (SRE-2359). ETA: 2 weeks.

Post-incident open questions and unknowns:
- What client retry patterns (SDK versions) exacerbate the feedback loop? Need to correlate client user agents.
- Is there a safe default breaker policy that prefers degraded streaming across all customers, or do some customers require strict failure vs degraded streaming?
- Could a staged rollout gate in the invalidator have prevented the fanout pattern? We need a deployment gate design doc.

Communication notes:
- Customer comms: initial notification sent at 13:30 UTC to affected customers via status.redwood.com (incident id RWI-20270408-01).
- Postmortem draft timeline: internal review by 2027-04-15, public summary for status page by 2027-04-20.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting checklist for on-call (one-page):
1) Identify whether problem is KV-lock heavy or pure network/backend.
2) If KV-lock heavy -> rollback invalidator change -> enable loader backoff -> widen breakers.
3) If backend 5xx -> check model pool saturation -> scale replicas, enable fallback routing.
4) Always: add debug sampling to a few affected sessions and preserve traces (trace id + logs).

Notes to self (informal):
- We almost had a quick mitigation by changing breaker policy earlier — add a runbook step to check breaker thresholds within first 10m next time.
- Keep a small canary for invalidator routing changes that exercises cross-region failover scenarios.
